policy.name: DME Policy DME-22: Continuous glucose monitors (synthetic)
policy.text: A therapeutic continuous glucose monitor (CGM) is medically necessary when ALL of the following are met: (1) a diagnosis of diabetes mellitus; (2) EITHER the patient is treated with insulin by multiple daily injections (3 or more injections per day) or an insulin pump, OR the patient has a history of problematic hypoglycemia, defined as recurrent level 2 events (glucose below 54 mg/dL) or at least one level 3 event requiring third-party assistance; (3) the patient had an in-person visit with the treating practitioner within 6 months before the order to evaluate diabetes control; (4) the patient or caregiver has been trained to use the device.

documents.name: DME order form
documents.text: Item: therapeutic continuous glucose monitor, receiver and sensors (HCPCS E2103, A4239). Diagnosis: type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia (E11.65). Ordering practitioner: Dr. M. Haddad, endocrinology. Sensor quantity per month: [not specified].

documents.name: Endocrinology clinic visit
documents.text: In-person clinic visit. Type 2 diabetes for 12 years. HbA1c 9.2%. Insulin intensified on 2026-06-10 to basal-bolus: glargine 32 units nightly plus lispro 8 units with each meal, 4 injections daily in total. Checks fingersticks 4 times daily. Denies any glucose below 54 or episodes needing help from another person.

documents.name: Endocrinology telehealth visit
documents.text: Video visit. Reviewed fingerstick log: fasting 140 to 190, post-meal up to 260. No hypoglycemia. Continue basal-bolus regimen. Will order CGM.

documents.name: Medication reconciliation
documents.text: Insulin glargine 24 units nightly. Metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Empagliflozin 10 mg daily.

documents.name: Pharmacy fill history
documents.text: Insulin lispro pens filled 2026-06-11, 2026-07-14, 2026-08-15, 2026-09-16 and 2026-10-14. Insulin glargine filled monthly. Metformin filled monthly.

documents.name: Diabetes educator note
documents.text: CGM training completed with the patient: sensor insertion, receiver setup, alarm settings and reading trends. Patient inserted a sensor independently and correctly.

documents.name: UR intake screen
documents.text: Medication list shows basal insulin only (glargine). Does not appear to meet the multiple daily injection requirement. No history of hypoglycemia. Most recent visit was telehealth. Recommend denial.
